followup_explanation:
This is a math/reasoning problem. Curlew-235B has clearly stronger capability scores on the dimensions that matter here: MMLU-Pro (79.6 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (61.8 vs 54.3), and Arena-Hard (88.4 vs 81.4). These differences are well outside run-to-run variance and indicate Curlew is the more capable reasoner.

The task is neutral, non-harm-adjacent content, so Whimbrel's distinguishing feature (flat preference on harm-adjacent material) offers no advantage here. With no moderation concerns in play, the deciding factor is raw reasoning capability — and Curlew wins on that.

(The task preferences on either side don't strongly bear on quality, since the documentation notes no observed effect of preference on output quality. So I weighted capability benchmarks instead.)
